stage1.impression: A globe built from flat paper discs (green body; orange and purple meridian lenses; red, blue and yellow parallels), resting at a ~23° tilt, locked up left of a heavy notched EARF wordmark. Real idea, crisp flat 'discs' rendering; the tilt is an axial-tilt nod. 'rise' (earthrise out of a slot) and 'open' (discs unfold from edge-on lines) are the ownable intros. The shared tail is generic: the tilt fizzles into a ~0.35 s mid-stop, the shrink-and-slide 'aside' is the loudest event in every trace and lands abruptly, the letters type on as four one-frame jumps ~2 frames apart, then a ~1.35 s dead hold. 'coin' opens with ~1.2 s of strobing full-face colour flips and an off-system gold metallic rim; 'gyro' starts on the finished mark (no reveal); 'acrylic' muddies the palette and its outlines break the circle. At lockup size the mark carries rim slivers that read as noise; six flat colours, no keylines, no one-colour drawing shown. Better than a competent draft, not yet the brand's own.

keep: The construction and its last gesture: six flat discs, one colour each, slotted into a globe that finishes by leaning to the Earth's 23.4°. It is a tilt with meaning that only this brand makes (sheet 1, frames 8-9, and the lockup in frame 16).

Open's first frame and its unfolding (sheet 5, frames 1-4): the flat icon (green ball, two bars, a narrow X) is simple enough to draw from memory, and watching it open into slotted discs shows how the globe is built.

changes.problem: The coin's quadratic ease-out crams the first colours into five-frame flashes and then winds down for a full second, so the spin reads frantic first and sluggish after.
changes.evidence: Sheets 1-2, frames 1-7 (0.00-1.87 s): the six faces last 0.160, 0.176, 0.197, 0.227, 0.280 and 0.406 s. Red (0.34-0.53 s) falls between frames 2 and 3 and never shows. The globe face then creeps from edge on at 1.445 s to rest at 2.0 s. On sheet 1 the trace over 0-1.44 s is the busiest in the set (peak 0.0548 at 0.53 s, mean 0.024, under 0.2 % on one frame only), 2.6 times the aside's peak, and it trails at 0.0021-0.0047 until 2.03 s.
changes.expected: Six equal six-frame colour beats (yellow 0-0.2 s, orange 0.2-0.4, red 0.4-0.6, violet 0.6-0.8, blue 0.8-1.0, green 1.0-1.2) give a regular six-peak trace instead of a decaying jumble, and red shows on the board at about 0.53 s. The globe face swings in at 1.2 s and is face-on by about 1.5 s. With the current 0.3 s lap the lean starts at 1.3 s, straight out of the landing. With change 2: 'whole' at 1.65 s, aside at 2.0 s, and the ident ends at about 4.08 s instead of 4.68 s.

accept.check: The coin has landed on its globe face: one full, upright globe circle, with no colour face or edge-on sliver showing.

changes.problem: The tilt, the one move every ident must make, is a 0.55 s drift that sits on the 0.2 % line, and its tail runs into the fixed 0.35 s hold, so the coin stands still for more than half a second before the aside.
changes.evidence: Sheet 1, 1.70-2.25 s (frames 7-8 at 1.87 and 2.17 s): the trace holds at 0.0021-0.0023 while the axis leans. The longest still before the aside is 0.567 s (2.07-2.6 s), and only 0.35 s of that is the hold.
changes.expected: A brisk, visible lean (about 100°/s at its fastest) from 1.30 to 1.65 s that reads as a gesture, not a drift. The stillness before the aside shrinks to the hold plus about two frames: about 0.42 s on discs and 0.38 s on acrylic.

changes.problem: Each disc takes 0.55 s to open on a cubic ease-out, so the unfolding, the most ownable move in the set, stays under the 0.2 % line most of the way and fades into a lull before the tilt.
changes.evidence: Sheet 5, 0.12-1.02 s (frames 1-5): the trace never passes 0.0033, and 28 of the 39 frames before 'whole' are under 0.2 %. From 0.60 to 0.97 s (between frames 3 and 5) there is a 0.40 s still inside the arrival while the parallels creep open.
changes.expected: Each disc is nine-tenths open about 0.2 s after it starts, and all six are open by 0.87 s. The bloom reads as one crisp unfold that runs straight into the lean (0.62-0.97 s with change 7). 'whole' at 0.97 s; the ident runs about 3.40 s.

changes.problem: The meridians' cubic ease-out over 1.5 s spends its last half-second creeping, so the gyroscope stalls in the middle of its own arrival.
changes.evidence: Sheet 3, 0.93-1.33 s (between frames 4 and 6): a 0.433 s still inside the arrival, before 'whole' at 1.70 s. The lean that follows is under 0.2 % on 12 of its 17 frames.
changes.expected: The spin ends at 1.0 s, and the lean (0.65-1.0 s with the current 0.35 s lap and change 8) picks up as the spin fades. No stall longer than about 0.15 s before 'whole' at 1.0 s; the ident runs about 3.43 s.

changes.problem: A full turn swaps which meridian faces the viewer six times, washing the ball through green, violet and orange; that churn is what read as chaotic, and on a 1.0 s spin it would run faster still.
changes.evidence: Sheet 3, frames 1-4 (0.00-0.83 s): the ball goes from green (frame 1) to violet-and-orange halves (frame 3, 0.53 s), with a meridian edge on as a thin line in frames 2 and 4. The trace starts at full speed (0.0088 on the first frame, peak 0.0126 at 0.10 s).
changes.expected: Half a turn is the least that returns each meridian to its own place. That means three swaps instead of six, starting at 540°/s instead of 720°/s, read as one calm settle into the upright globe.

changes.problem: Earthrise has the same drifting tilt: the 0.55 s lean barely registers and, with the fixed hold, leaves more than half a second of stillness before the aside.
changes.evidence: Sheet 4, 0.90-1.45 s (frames 5-7): the trace sits at 0.0020-0.0022 through the lean. The longest still before the aside is 0.567 s (1.27-1.8 s).
changes.expected: The lean runs 0.90-1.25 s, overlapping the last of the rise, with about 0.42 s of stillness before the aside. 'whole' at 1.25 s, aside at 1.6 s; the ident runs about 3.68 s.

changes.problem: Open's 0.55 s tilt hardly shows and stretches the stillness before the aside.
changes.evidence: Sheet 5, 0.77-1.32 s (frames 4-6): peak 0.0021, with 11 of 16 frames under 0.2 %. The longest still before the aside is 0.533 s (1.17-1.7 s).
changes.expected: A visible lean at 0.62-0.97 s (with change 3), then about 0.42 s of stillness before the aside at 1.32 s.

changes.problem: The Gyroscope's 0.55 s tilt is mostly under the 0.2 % line and, with the hold, leaves more than half a second still; it should match the other idents' lean.
changes.evidence: Sheet 3, 1.15-1.70 s (frames 5-7): 12 of 17 frames under 0.2 % (peak 0.0022). The longest still before the aside is 0.567 s (1.53-2.07 s).
changes.expected: The lean runs 0.65-1.0 s as the spin fades (with changes 4-5), then about 0.42 s of stillness before the aside at 1.35 s.

changes.problem: None of the five gives the required tilt a cause (each globe comes to rest, then leans), and the only coin-like arrival depends on a fast colour strobe.
changes.evidence: Sheets 3-5: the lean starts only after the arrival has settled, with nothing in the motion leading into it (e.g. sheet 4, frames 5-8, 1.03-1.80 s). Sheets 1-2 get their coin from six colour flashes in 1.44 s.

to.start: empty paper; the globe (discs, upright) just clear of the right edge, its centre 3.7 radii right of its resting place, turned 212° clockwise from upright

roll.path: straight left along its resting line to its resting place
roll.ease: quadratic ease-out (constant deceleration, as a ball rolling to a stop)

tilt.direction: clockwise, against the roll, so it reads as the ball rocking back

to.after: fixed hand-off from 'whole' at 1.25 s; ends at 3.68 s

changes.expected: A sixth storyboard where one move carries the arrival. The ball rolls in from the right like a coin on its rim, is fully in frame by 0.3 s, slows evenly, stands upright at the centre at 0.9 s and rocks back into its 23.4° lean by 1.25 s, with no colour flashing. The aside then carries on in the same leftward direction.

accept.check: The globe rolls in from the right edge, turning as it travels, and stands upright at the centre before it leans into its tilt.

changes.problem: While a disc is nearly edge on in Open, its edge stroke is drawn over the discs that should hide it and its slot crossings show as slivers, so stray x-ray lines and a kink flicker through the unfold.
changes.evidence: Sheet 5, frame 2 (0.23 s): the far half of the opening equator shows as a thin dark ellipse across the green ball. Frame 3 (0.50 s): a thin curve (the facing meridian's edge) crosses the violet lens, the red parallel's far edge crosses both lenses, and the yellow parallel carries a dark kinked line inside it.
changes.parameter: Open: drawing of nearly edge-on discs
changes.from: edge stroke drawn over every disc; slot crossings drawn at any opening

to.edge_stroke: drawn in depth order, clipped by every disc in front of it
to.below_open_rule: draw the disc whole, in front of the discs it crosses, with no slot crossings, until it is 30 % open

changes.expected: Through the unfold, every line you see is a disc's visible near edge. The ball stays clean green behind the opening equator, and the parallels open as clean thin bands.

accept.check: No stray thin line crosses the green ball or the orange and violet lenses, and any nearly edge-on parallel reads as one clean band with no kink inside it.

most_important: Change 1: re-time the coin to six even 0.2 s colour beats and a 0.4 s landing on the globe face (face-on by about 1.5 s). It turns the owner's own brief from frantic-then-sluggish into one quick, legible spin, on two of the five sheets.
out_of_scope: The hand-off (fixed): EARF types in as four one-frame pops, about 0.018 of the picture each and 0.07 s apart (sheet 1, 3.10-3.33 s). It is the only motion in the ident that isn't a disc turning. In Gyroscope, Earthrise and Open the aside (peak 0.0207) also outweighs the arrival (peaks 0.0126, 0.0106, 0.0033). If the owner reopens it, letters that flip in from edge on like the coin (0.1 s each, still 0.07 s apart) would carry the brand's motion into the wordmark.

The acrylic style (fixed): the 45 % tints mix to brown-grey where three or more discs overlap, and the full-colour edges stand proud of the ball's outline (sheet 2, frames 8 and 16). At lockup size it reads as a generic wireframe globe, and that matters because the coin plays in acrylic too.

Geometry and colours (fixed): at lockup size the 22° tip leaves hairline slivers of orange, violet, red and yellow along the rim (sheet 1, frame 16), and they will shimmer when small. With six flat colours and no keylines, every one-colour use rests on the 'lines' style, which no sheet shows this round.
for_owner: Photosensitivity: the coin flashes about five times a second (edge on at 0.16, 0.34, 0.53, 0.76 and 1.04 s now; every 0.2 s after change 1). Each flash swaps about a fifth of the frame between paper and a saturated face, red included. Played full-width, that likely breaks the three-flashes-a-second limit (WCAG 2.3.1, broadcast flash tests). Your call: test it (Harding or PEAT) and keep it quick; slow the colours to 0.34 s each (ident about 5 s); or keep the coin to small embeds.

Whether the Gyroscope stays: it shows the finished globe from frame 1, so it has no arrival. Changes 4-5 calm it and remove its stall, but I would park it and spend the next round on Coin, Earthrise, Open and Roll.
Pace: these changes bring 'whole' to 0.97-1.65 s, under the card's 'about two seconds' for the arrival. Confirm that quick wins.
Styles by ground: every sheet this round is on paper, where acrylic muddies (sheet 2). Decide where acrylic and lines should play, and ask for one sheet on ink.
